Since triamterene is a known inhibitor of the same subunit, this creates a chain of interactions where amiloride indirectly influences the activity of the subunit through its effect on triamterene. Additionally, amiloride has been shown to target another subunit, the Voltage-dependent N-type calcium channel subunit alpha-1B, which is also a target of triamterene. This indicates that amiloride may exert its effects on the subunit through multiple pathways, possibly by modulating the activity of triamterene or other related compounds. The evidence suggests a possible mechanism by which amiloride could influence the function of Voltage-dependent calcium channel subunit alpha-2/delta-3, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
